newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: World Bank to decide in a wk on Lithuania credits.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to decide in a wk on Lithuania credits.

text.p: A visiting World Bank mission will decide in one week if Lithuania is meeting its obligations under agreements for structural adjustment credits from the Bank, the Lituanian government said on Tuesday.
The mission's assessment is crucial to the release of a second $40-million tranche of an $80-million credit aimed at reforms to the energy, banking and agricultural sectors.

A local World Bank representative told Reuters the main criteria attached to the credits included establishment of real market prices for heating, electric energy and gas, decentralisation of the energy sector and privatisation of three state-owned banks and agricultural import tariffs.

"Along with the banking sector, the World Bank is interested in changes in Lithuania's energy sector, agriculture and especially, in government policy in defending its market by applying customs tariffs", the government said in a statement.
Lithuania's energy sector remains heavily subsidised, which means consumers there do not pay world prices for their energy.

On Monday, the IMF and Lithuania failed to agree on reducing import tariffs. Lithuania wanted to slow the rate at which it cuts tariffs, but the IMF said the country should stick to earlier agreements.
